text: Sebaste stood on the hill of old Samaria, capital of the northern kingdom. Herod the Great crowned it with a temple to the emperor.
I met him at Jacob’s well, years ago. He asked me for a drink. Sit down, scribe. He would.
A Samaritan family has taken Philip in, and they want you at their table too. Their bread is Samaritan bread. Every rule you were taught says you do not eat it.

You left Jerusalem by night with Philip and a handful of others. Three days north, the road climbs to the city Herod rebuilt and named for Augustus. You have never set foot in a Samaritan city. You were raised to walk around them.
I met him at Jacob’s well, years ago. He asked me for a drink. Sit down, daughter. He would.
Philip does not go back to Jerusalem with them. He says the Lord has something else for him, and that you should come.
The bread is good. Nobody chokes. Philip catches your eye and smiles.

Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and proclaimed to them the Christ. The multitudes listened with one accord to the things that were spoken by Philip, when they heard and saw the signs which he did.

But there was a certain man, Simon by name, who used to practice sorcery in the city, and amazed the people of Samaria, making himself out to be some great one, to whom they all listened, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is that great power of God.” They listened to him, because for a long time he had amazed them with his sorceries.
Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
For unclean spirits came out of many of those who had them. They came out, crying with a loud voice. Many who had been paralyzed and lame were healed.

But when they believed Philip preaching good news concerning the Kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women. Simon himself also believed. Being baptized, he continued with Philip. Seeing signs and great miracles occurring, he was amazed.

Now when Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money, saying, “Give me also this power, that whoever I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit.”
They therefore, when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the Good News to many villages of the Samaritans.

Now when the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them, who, when they had come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit; for as yet he had fallen on none of them. They had only been baptized in the name of Christ Jesus.
There was great joy in that city.
Simon answered, “Pray for me to the Lord, that none of the things which you have spoken happen to me.”

But Peter said to him, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money! You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart isn’t right before God. Repent therefore of this, your wickedness, and ask God if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you. For I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and in the bondage of iniquity.”
